extraFacts.fact: A stockless anchor has no stock (cross-bar) across the shank, so it can be drawn into a hawse pipe and stowed against the hull.
extraFacts.source: ISO 1704, Ships and marine technology - Stockless anchors (terminology and scope)

extraFacts.fact: A drag embedment (fluke) anchor is installed by dragging it along the seabed until the flukes dig in, and holds by the resistance of the soil; its holding capacity depends on the soil type, the fluke angle and the penetration depth.
extraFacts.source: DNV-RP-E301, Design and installation of fluke anchors

extraFacts.fact: A mushroom anchor has a bell-shaped head that sinks into soft seabed sediment and holds by its weight and the surrounding soil, and is used for permanent moorings.
extraFacts.source: US Naval Facilities Engineering Command, Design Manual DM-26.5, Fleet Moorings
